newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FANS SALUTE LEYLAND IN HIS FINAL PITTSBURGH HOME GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FANS SALUTE LEYLAND IN HIS FINAL PITTSBURGH HOME GAME.

text.p: It was a Pittsburgh moment -- a Pirates defeat, followed by a 10-minute standing ovation for manager Jim Leyland.

Pinch-hitter Willie McGee's sacrifice fly scored Royce Clayton in the top of the 11th inning to lift the St Louis Cardinals to an 8-7 victory Wednesday, but all the fans cared about was that it was Leyland's final home game in Pittsburgh.

Leyland, who led Pittsburgh to three straight National League East titles from 1990-92, announced his resignation last week, saying he wants to manage a team with a chance to win soon. The perennially cost-cutting Pirates end the season with four games at Chicago.

Leyland received a standing ovation when he brought out the lineup card and each time he made a pitching change. The video screen played a tribute to Leyland in the middle of the fifth inning and he received the long standing ovation at the end of the game.

"I don't know how to explain," said Leyland, who turned down the team's offer for a formal ceremony. "I said all along I don't want anything special. No one could have planned anything that touched me as much as I was touched tonight.
"Not only a great season-ending crowd on a school night, but they stayed. I think that pretty much shows how they feel. That was unbelievable."

"I'm thrilled to have seen it in person," said St Louis manager Tony La Russa, who embraced Leyland at home plate after the game. "The fans may think he's great but those that know him, he's even better than that."
The Pirates have lost three in a row after a season-high 11-game winning streak.

In Los Angeles, Eric Karros snapped an eighth-inning tie with a solo homer, his 34th, as the Dodgers overcame a five-run deficit and beat the San Francisco Giants 7-5 to widen their National League West lead.
The Dodgers pulled 2 1/2 games ahead of San Diego and reduced their magic number to two for clinching a second consecutive division title.
The Dodgers take on the Giants one more time Thursday before hosting the pursuing Padres in a season-ending three-game series.
Scott Radinsky (5-1) got the win with a scoreless eighth. Closer Todd Worrell notched his major league-leading 44th save with a hitless ninth.
San Francisco's Barry Bonds broke a National League record by drawing his 149th walk this season, surpassing the mark set by Eddie Stanky in 1945 and tied by Jim Wynn in 1969.

Bonds also stole two bases, giving him 39. Bonds, who has 42 home runs, is on the verge of joining Jose Canseco as the only members of the 40-40 club. Canseco had 42 home runs and 40 stolen bases in 1988.
In San Diego, Ellis Burks drove in three runs with a homer, his 39th, and a double and Quinton McCracken added a solo homer as the Colorado Rockies defeated the Padres 5-3.
With Montreal's loss earlier in the evening the Padres continued to hold a 1 1/2 game lead over the Expos for the wild-card berth.
Colorado, which owns the worst road record in the majors at 28-53, has won two straight away from Coors Field.

In Philadelphia, David West and two relievers combined on a four-hitter and Ruben Amaro's single in the fourth plated the go-ahead run as the Phillies dealt the Montreal Expos their fifth loss in six games, 3-1.
West (2-2), who was hampered by injuries all season, made his first start in a month and allowed one run and two hits in six innings. He struck out six and did not walk a batter.
Ken Ryan gave up one hit and struck out one over two innings before Ricky Bottalico allowed one hit in the ninth but earned his 33rd save.
At Florida, major-league ERA leader Kevin Brown scattered five hits over seven innings and Jeff Conine had a run-scoring double as the Marlins blanked the Atlanta Braves 3-0.
Brown (17-11) struck out two and walked none as his ERA fell to 1.89. Robb Nen allowed one hit over the final 1 1/3 innings for his 34th save.
Tom Glavine (15-10) retired the first 10 batters before Edgar Renteria singled, stole second, took third on a wild pitch and scored on Conine's double.
Florida, which leads the majors with 13 shutouts, has won five straight.
In Cincinnati, Willie Greene's two-run homer in the third inning, his 17th of the season and fourth in two games, capped a four-run third inning as the Reds beat the Chicago Cub 4-3.
Brian McRae hit a solo homer for the Cubs.

In Houston, pinch-hitter Mike Simms singled in Craig Biggio in the bottom of the 10th as the Astros overcame a 4-0 deficit and snapped a season-high nine-game losing streak with a 5-4 victory over the New York Mets.
Butch Huskey, Matt Franco and Lance Johnson homered for New York.
